why_angle: The cited Synology pages give Hyper Backup's destination rules, and the rival answer gives two purchase prices. None of them gives a power draw, a yearly running cost or a payback time against cloud storage for a box left on all year at someone else's house. This page prices each candidate's waiting-state draw at the EIA August 2026 rate and works out how many months each box takes to beat Backblaze B2. On that basis the cheapest box to buy, the DS124, is also the cheapest to run.

page.after:
What the differences mean

Each yearly figure is watts × 8,760 hours, priced at the US residential average of 18.16¢/kWh for August 2026 (EIA). None of the figures include the drive's cost.

  • DS124: 3.44 W × 8.76 = 30.1 kWh a year with the drive hibernating, about $5.47. At Synology's 10.69 W access figure all day and night it would be 93.6 kWh, about $17.01.
  • DS223j: 4 W × 8.76 = 35.0 kWh hibernating, about $6.36. At its 16.31 W access figure, 142.9 kWh, about $25.95.
  • TerraMaster F2-212: PC-WELT's 3.9 W asleep × 8.76 = 34.2 kWh, about $6.20. Left at its 14.7 W idle, 128.8 kWh, about $23.38.
  • UGREEN DH2300: 10 W (the middle of OC Inside's 9–11 W idle) × 8.76 = 87.6 kWh, about $15.91. Neither OC Inside nor NASCompares measured it with the drives spun down, so plan on the idle figure.
  • Payback against B2 at 4 TB: B2 would bill 4 × $6.95 = $27.80 a month. For the DH2300: $239.99 ÷ ($27.80 − $15.91 ÷ 12) = 9.1 months. The same sum with each box's Amazon price on 2026-11-13 gives 5.9 months for the DS124, 6.2 for the F2-212 and 7.7 for the DS223j.
  • Small backups: at 1 TB, B2 bills $6.95 a month, and the DS124 takes about 25 months to pay back. Below 1 TB, cloud stays cheaper for more than two years.

What a backup target costs to keep running

A remote target works for perhaps an hour a night and waits the rest of the day. Its running cost is set by what it draws while waiting, not by its access figure. Synology publishes a drive-hibernation draw for both of its boxes: 3.44 W for the DS124 and 4 W for the DS223j. PC-WELT's wall measurement of the F2-212 shows what sleep is worth: 3.9 W asleep against 14.7 W idle, about 73% less. A box whose drives hibernate between nightly runs costs about a third as much to run as one that idles all day.

Features matter as much as watts. Synology's Hyper Backup spec lists only a remote Synology NAS or Synology C2 Storage as destinations for entire-system backup. Rsync servers and S3-compatible clouds take folder and package backups. The DS124 runs DSM 7.4, and the current Hyper Backup Vault release (4.2.2-4262, 2026-07-07) requires DSM 7.3 or later, so it can host Vault. The TerraMaster and UGREEN boxes join as rsync servers instead. TerraMaster's TOS has an rsync Server under Control Panel › Network Services › File Services, and NASCompares lists rsync among the DH2300's protocols on UGOS Pro. Any destination needs at least 8 GB free. Hyper Backup keeps up to 65,535 versions and offers AES-256 client-side encryption.

Not recommended

A used Synology DS216j as the Vault box. Synology's Download Center lists DSM 7.1 as the newest release for it. Hyper Backup Vault 4.2.2 requires DSM 7.3, so a DS216j can't run the current Vault. Before you buy any used Synology for this job, check that its Download Center page offers DSM 7.3 or later.
